rows.question: Who must approve a regular work location change?
rows.answer: Employees must receive manager approval before changing their regular work location. A temporary change within the same country for fewer than 15 business days may be approved by the manager, but longer changes require People Operations review.

citations.citation_text: Employees must receive manager approval before changing their regular work location. A temporary change within the same country for fewer than 15 business days may be approved by the manager. Longer changes require People Operations review.

retrieved_chunks.content_preview:
Approval Requirements

Employees must receive manager approval before changing their regular work location. A temporary change within the same country for fewer than 15 business days may be approved by the manager. Longer changes require People Operations review.

Managers should consider team coverage, customer needs, time zone overlap, and data handling requirements before approving remote work.

Cross-Border Work

Northstar does not guarantee approval for work from any country. Temporary cross-border work requires People Operations review before travel. The company does not maintain a formal visa or immigration policy in the employee knowledge base.

Requests to work outside Canada or the United States are considered ambiguous until People Operations reviews tax, employment, and security implications.

Work Model

Northstar supports hybrid work and approved remote work. Employees assigned to Toronto, Montreal, or New York offices are expected to attend office collaboration days when scheduled by their department.

Remote employees may work from approved locations in Canada or the United States if their role, tax location, and security requirements support remote work.

Approved Use

Northstar systems must be used for company business, approved learning, customer support, and authorized operational work. Employees may use company devices for limited personal use if it does not interfere with work, create security risk, or violate policy.

Vacation Approval Workflow

Vacation requests of 1 to 5 business days should be submitted at least 10 business days in advance. Requests longer than 5 business days should be submitted at least 20 business days in advance.

Managers approve vacation based on business coverage, project deadlines, and fairness across the team. Managers should not deny vacation without explaining the business reason.

rows.question: What is the annual wellness stipend amount?
rows.answer: Eligible full-time employees receive an annual wellness stipend of 750 CAD or 550 USD per calendar year, based on payroll country.

citations.citation_text: Eligible full-time employees receive a wellness stipend of 750 CAD or 550 USD per calendar year, based on payroll country.

retrieved_chunks.content_preview:
Wellness Stipend

Eligible full-time employees receive a wellness stipend of 750 CAD or 550 USD per calendar year, based on payroll country. The stipend may be used for fitness memberships, mental health apps, ergonomic equipment, or wellness programs.

Unused wellness stipend amounts do not carry over into the next calendar year.

Health Benefits

Northstar provides health, dental, and vision benefits to eligible full-time employees. Coverage begins on the first day of the month after the employee's start date. Plan details vary by employee location.

This overview does not include provider contracts, claim adjudication rules, or legal advice about benefits eligibility.

Retirement Matching

Northstar offers retirement contribution matching after 3 months of service. The company match is up to 4% of eligible earnings, subject to payroll country rules and plan eligibility.

Exact compensation formulas and salary bands are not included in this benefits overview.

Learning Budget

Employees receive an annual learning budget of 1,500 CAD or 1,100 USD for approved courses, books, conferences, and certifications related to their role. Manager approval is required before purchase.

Learning budget requests should include the business purpose and expected outcome. The learning budget is separate from required compliance training.

Missing Policy Areas

Northstar does not publish a sabbatical policy in the employee knowledge base. Employees asking about sabbaticals should contact People Operations.

rows.answer: I could not find this in the available documents.

Account Sharing

Employees must not share passwords, MFA codes, access tokens, or accounts. Each employee is responsible for activity performed under their account.

Sharing Rules

Employees may share data only with people who have a business need and appropriate access. Confidential and Restricted data must not be shared in public channels or with unapproved external recipients.

Sales materials may be shared externally only when marked as customer-approved or public-facing.

Company Devices

Employees who regularly access company systems should use a company-managed device. Company devices must have disk encryption, endpoint protection, automatic screen lock, and current operating system updates.

Employees may not disable security tools or remove device management controls from company devices.

Personal Devices

Personal devices may be used for limited work access only when enrolled in approved mobile device management or when access occurs through approved browser-based tools. Personal devices must use a passcode, supported operating system, and automatic lock.

Restricted data must not be downloaded to personal devices. Confidential data should be accessed only through approved company systems.

Prohibited Behavior

Employees must not attempt to bypass security controls, scan systems without approval, copy customer data to personal storage, or use company systems for illegal, harassing, or discriminatory activity.

rows.question: Who should I contact for PTO questions and what is the basic vacation entitlement?
rows.answer: Based on limited supporting evidence, For PTO questions, you should contact People Operations. Full-time employees receive 20 paid vacation days per calendar year, accrued monthly and usable after the first 30 days of employment. Part-time employees receive prorated vacation based on scheduled weekly hours. Employees may carry over up to 5 unused vacation days into the next calendar year, which must be used by March 31 or they expire unless local law requires otherwise.

retrieved_chunks.content_preview:
Vacation Entitlement

Full-time employees receive 20 paid vacation days per calendar year. Vacation is accrued monthly and may be used after the employee's first 30 days of employment. Part-time employees receive prorated vacation based on scheduled weekly hours.

Employees may carry over up to 5 unused vacation days into the next calendar year. Carried-over days must be used by March 31 or they expire unless local law requires a different outcome.

Related Policies

For time off, consult the PTO and Leave Policy. For remote work, consult the Remote and Hybrid Work Policy. For acceptable technology use, consult the Acceptable Use Policy.

Vacation Approval Workflow

Vacation requests of 1 to 5 business days should be submitted at least 10 business days in advance. Requests longer than 5 business days should be submitted at least 20 business days in advance.

Managers approve vacation based on business coverage, project deadlines, and fairness across the team. Managers should not deny vacation without explaining the business reason.

Employee Support Channels

General HR questions should be sent to People Operations. Benefits questions should be sent to the benefits support queue. Security access questions should be sent to IT Support. Performance or role expectation questions should first be discussed with the employee's manager.

Parental Leave Summary

Eligible full-time employees may receive up to 12 weeks of company-supported parental leave after 6 months of service. Local statutory benefits may apply separately. Employees should contact People Operations at least 60 days before the expected leave date when possible.

This document provides a company policy summary and does not provide legal advice.

rows.question: How should I position Northstar against BI tools while avoiding prohibited claims?
rows.answer: Based on limited supporting evidence, You should position Northstar against generic BI tools by emphasizing that Northstar is workflow-aware analytics, which connects metrics to approvals, queues, owners, and operational follow-up, whereas generic BI tools primarily report metrics. An approved response is: "Northstar complements BI by helping operations teams act on workflow issues, not just view dashboards." While doing so, avoid prohibited claims such as guaranteeing revenue improvement, replacing all existing systems, meeting every regulatory requirement, or promising committed roadmap features.

Positioning Against Generic BI Tools

When compared with generic BI tools, position Northstar as workflow-aware analytics. Generic BI tools can report metrics, but Northstar connects metrics to approvals, queues, owners, and operational follow-up.

Approved response: "Northstar complements BI by helping operations teams act on workflow issues, not just view dashboards."

Prohibited Claims

Sales Representatives must not claim that Northstar guarantees revenue improvement, replaces all existing systems, meets every regulatory requirement, or has committed roadmap features. Customer names and confidential deal details should not be shared.

Positioning Against Workflow Tools

When compared with workflow-only tools, position Northstar as analytics plus process visibility. Workflow tools coordinate tasks, while Northstar tracks patterns, bottlenecks, and KPI impact across workflows.

Approved Talk Track

Northstar helps operations leaders see where work slows down, which approvals are delayed, and which data quality issues affect business reporting. Sales Representatives should avoid promising product roadmap commitments.

Product Limitations

Northstar is not a replacement for a system of record, identity provider, ERP, or clinical decision system. Sales Representatives should not promise unsupported integrations, exact roadmap delivery dates, or customer-specific contract commitments.

rows.question: How should a manager handle ongoing performance concerns?

Performance Improvement Process

When serious performance issues continue after feedback, managers should consult People Operations before starting a formal performance improvement process. Documentation should include expectations, timeline, support offered, and review checkpoints.

This guide does not contain salary bands or compensation formulas.

Conflict Handling

Managers should address team conflict early, document observed behavior, and avoid making unsupported conclusions about intent. Repeated conduct concerns should be discussed with People Operations.

Performance Documentation

Performance feedback should include specific examples, business impact, expected behavior, and follow-up actions. Managers should avoid vague labels and should distinguish between skill gaps, behavior concerns, and role mismatch.

One-on-One Expectations

Managers should hold one-on-one meetings with direct reports at least every two weeks. Notes should focus on priorities, blockers, feedback, and growth needs. Sensitive personal details should not be recorded unless required for an HR process.

Review Cycle

Northstar runs formal performance reviews twice per year: mid-year review in June and year-end review in December. Managers should collect evidence throughout the review period instead of relying only on recent events.
